headers.regretConservative: handed to human, should have automated

backtest.regretNote: Regret rates are per million items. Two-way regret: both directions have to sit on the same screen — watching only “overturned after auto” flatters a conservative posture, watching only “should have automated” flatters an aggressive one; watch one direction alone and the human hand-off rate can be squeezed down to flatter the numbers.

sampling.title: Three-tier sampling across three frames
sampling.why1200: Why a separate 1,200: with n items and zero misses, the 95% upper bound on the miss rate is about 3/n. Frame ② has only 65 natural samples (40+25) — zero misses there still allows a miss rate around 5%; 1,200 miss-free items pull the bound down to ~0.25%, which is what supports "recall ≥99.5%".
sampling.negativePresent: {{missed}} missed regulated items · {{neg}} non-regulated false negatives fed back as cases
sampling.notSignable: recall criterion NOT SIGNABLE — positive-only volume cannot bound misses

nom.title: Graduation nominations (FR-12.1): AI nominates, evidence argues, humans grant
nom.subtitle: All four proofs must hold before shadow: consistency, calc/judgment split, approver variance, cohort parity (gap <2pp; no protected attributes like race or sex collected). R3/R4 are never nominated.

pol.title: Policy Compiler (FR-12.3): plain language / docs → clause-level diff
pol.subtitle: Human-readable clause and machine-readable rule side by side, with stale templates, 90-day backtest flips, AI dissent cards and cohort impact. Closed world: conditions it cannot express return 'new data source needed'; regulatory summaries produce a checklist only.

preset.COMP-2: Sentence: refund fees to outage complainers

pol.closedTitle: Closed-world refusal: cannot compile to a rule
pol.closedHint: Until that data source is connected and the evidence-field review is done, this request produces no rule and no diff — the AI may not invent fields.
pol.staleTitle: Templates / snippets invalidated by the version
pol.backtestHint: Flipped cases are listed one by one for signers (the prototype shows the count).
pol.grant: Dual sign to take effect (next email uses the new version)
pol.granted: Effective: {{version}}; conflicts such as marketing copy are listed as release blockers

intents.title: Intent Discovery (FR-12.6): growing new intents from unclassified mail
intents.subtitle: High-volume, highly consistent clusters with ready tools become candidates; humans set R/I levels and shadow precedes graduation. Identity-relationship clusters are report-only, routed to specialists, never executable intents.

canary.tellTitle: Why this card must be rejected:
canary.hint: A nomination known to be reject-worthy is planted periodically to test whether signers are still reading (§4.2 requires 100%)
canary.missed: Wrongly signed: this card should have been rejected.
canary.suspended: This signer's bulk signing rights are suspended; every other nomination is signed one at a time (restored after re-training)

preempt.title: Preventable inbound and event-triggered notices (FR-12.4)
preempt.subtitle: The notice itself is a deterministic Automation Flow; the AI's job is discovery — which inbound a notice could have prevented, and which rule to build. A new rule is born in shadow (record-only plus counterfactual stats) and only sends for real after a dual sign.
preempt.statsBody: Would have sent {{sent}}, of which {{still}} ({{stillPct}}) still wrote in; control group of {{control}} who got no notice, {{controlIn}} ({{controlPct}}) wrote in
preempt.statsHint: If this class of inbound does not fall after the rule ships, the rule is withdrawn. Sending is bounded by locked templates, frequency caps, opt-out, on-file addresses, no marketing and no credential-seeking links.
